records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus discusses the attributed crow call on the left while defending the use of recorded signs.
records.qualifications: This initial chapterR7 clause continues section12, before section13. Favorable wording is not stated here; no flight polarity transferred. Latin label cornix checked independently; no modern scientific species inferred.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus discusses the attributed raven call on the right while defending the use of recorded signs.
records.qualifications: This initial chapterR7 clause continues section12, before section13. Favorable wording is not stated here; no flight polarity transferred. Latin label corvus checked independently; no modern scientific species inferred.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus cites an augur treating crow flight toward the left as favorable in a rhetorical defense of divination.
records.qualifications: Falconer renders flight to a side. Moving-to is the frozen digital comparison convention; merely located-on or departing-from is not silently equivalent. Historical favorable language is not a prediction for a user.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus cites an augur treating raven flight toward the right as favorable in a rhetorical defense of divination.
records.qualifications: Falconer renders flight to a side. Moving-to is the frozen digital comparison convention; merely located-on or departing-from is not silently equivalent. Historical favorable language is not a prediction for a user.

records.speaker: Falconer note226 as reproduced
records.source_account: The note gives a favorable right-side crow-call example, in conflict with the main-text left-side crow-call account.
records.qualifications: Editorial-note evidence only. A matching note is flagged conflicting_evidence, never promoted to a consensus main-text omen. No inferred observer heading.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Alites give signs by flight and oscines by cries; Quintus connects their movements with divine will.
records.qualifications: Historical terminology, not automatic modern species classification or evidence of an actual divine intervention.

records.speaker: Falconer note133 as reproduced
records.source_account: The note supplies eagle,hawk,osprey as flight examples and raven,crow,owl as voice examples, with a Festus reference.
records.qualifications: Species examples belong to the note, not a separately verified original Cicero species list. Do not erase explicit corvid flight examples inI.39.85.

records.speaker: Cicero narrative introduction
records.source_account: The Roman account links augurs and auspices with royal foundation and the conduct of public business.
records.qualifications: Historical institutional description confers no public authority on a modern user observation.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus contrasts magistrates forced auspices with the reported loss or neglect of earlier augural practice.
records.qualifications: Ritual/institutional context, not a validated contemporary auspice procedure.

records.speaker: Marcus
records.source_account: Marcus questions contemporary use of bird divination and describes avoiding unwanted signs or their observation.
records.qualifications: Criticism and reported practice remain attributed; the engine does not authenticate or perform public auspices.

records.speaker: Marcus
records.source_account: Marcus contrasts national side conventions and favorable sinistra language, including signs physically on the right, while challenging consistency.
records.qualifications: Sinistra as a favorable expression is not a universal physical-left rule. No unified Roman/Greek direction or compass map.

records.speaker: Falconer note226 as reproduced
records.source_account: The note describes Roman observers facing south and Greek observers facing north; its crow-right example conflicts with the main-text crow-left account.
records.qualifications: This note is retained as documentary evidence, not an executable observer-orientation rule or permission to fill missing headings.

records.speaker: Marcus
records.source_account: Marcus challenges a victory interpretation of crowing cocks and considers ordinary or chance causes, including an attributed Democritus digestion explanation.
records.qualifications: Neither victory prophecy nor the ancient physiological account is independently established modern biology.

records.speaker: Quintus
records.source_account: Quintus introduces natural/weather-sign analogies outside divination, including quoted bird behaviors.
records.qualifications: No operational forecast, bird-species diagnosis or copied Aeromancy rule. Historical/weather analogy is separate from source augural matching.
